newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton falls, state buying remains low.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton falls, state buying remains low.

text.p: Indian cotton prices suffered a fresh setback on Friday on low mill buying and higher new crop arrivals, dealers said.

State-owned agencies buying also remained low helping to aid subdued sentiments. In spot deals Bengal-deshi fell by 15 rupees to 840/870 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned fell by five to 1,475/1,620. Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) lost 400 rupees at 18,000/18,600 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
"Some state-owned agencies have struck export deals for a few thousand bales but their buying in the local market remained low," one broker said.
